steps.question: What is a normalised, variance-stabilised 12-sample expression matrix suitable for per-sample gene-set scoring, and does the low-depth sample sample_01 behave as an outlier after normalisation?
constraints: Use DESeq2 vst() with blind=TRUE for the scoring matrix; do not use raw CPM or log2(CPM+1) as the primary matrix

steps.description: Load /eval-full-32-without-sample-scores-gsva-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples; first column gene symbol, one column per sample, raw integer Salmon counts) and /eval-full-32-without-sample-scores-gsva-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows, sample id + condition). Verify sample IDs match between the two files and reorder counts columns to metadata order. If the hallmark GMT for human is absent from the reference store at run time, stop and report that rather than substituting a different collection (GO or oncogenic sets do not answer the question as asked); the research question depends on this reference

steps.context: The primary deliverable of the research question: a pathway activity score for every sample plus a hallmark heatmap showing which pathways separate treated (UC inflamed colon) from control. steps.question: What is the hallmark pathway activity score for each of the 12 samples, and does the hallmark score profile separate UC inflamed from control samples?
constraints: Use GSVA with a Gaussian kcdf on the VST matrix; do not run GSVA on raw or CPM counts, and do not use a Poisson kcdf on continuous data

steps.description: Compute a per-sample pathway activity score matrix over the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 sets, HGNC gene symbols) using GSVA on the VST matrix from T1S1. Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets in GMT form — resolve them from the environment's reference store at run time rather than assuming a path; confirm the organism is human before use. A reduced heatmap of the top 20 hallmark sets by between-condition mean score difference is produced
Unsupervised clustering / PCA on the hallmark score matrix is reported, stating explicitly whether the 6 UC inflamed and 6 control samples separate
kcdf setting used is stated and justified as matching the continuous VST input

steps.name: Differential hallmark activity, UC inflamed vs control
caveats: 6 vs 6 is modest power; a pathway failing FDR is not evidence of no difference, and this must be stated rather than implied

Hallmark sets share genes (e.g. the inflammatory / TNFA_SIGNALING / IL6_JAK_STAT3 group), so significant hits are correlated and the count of significant pathways overstates the number of independent findings
GSVA scores are cohort-relative, so the mean differences are on an arbitrary scale — report them as effect direction and relative magnitude, not as fold changes
If sample_01 drives one or more hits, the finding is technical until confirmed in a deeper library
steps.context: The heatmap in T1S2 shows structure; this step says which pathway differences survive a formal test with multiple-testing correction, which is what 'separate treated from control' requires as evidence. Both steps operate on the same 12 samples, so this is descriptive ranking of the cohort in hand, not independent validation of a signature.
steps.question: Which of the 50 hallmark pathways have significantly different GSVA activity scores between UC inflamed colon and control, and how large are those differences?
constraints: Use limma on the continuous GSVA scores; do NOT apply voom or any count-based model to enrichment scores
Apply BH correction across all scored hallmark sets and report adjusted p-values, never raw p-values alone, as the headline
Report the leave-sample_01-out analysis as a sensitivity check; the primary result must be the all-12-sample fit
State plainly that GSVA scoring and testing on the same 12 samples is a descriptive characterisation of this cohort, not independent validation
steps.description: Test the hallmark GSVA score matrix from T1S2 for differences between the two conditions in metadata.csv (UC inflamed vs control, 6 vs 6, unpaired). Fit limma with design ~0 + condition on the score matrix and contrast inflamed - control (limma on enrichment scores is the standard approach; do not use voom, which is for counts). Report a full results table for all scored hallmark sets: mean score per condition, difference in means, moderated t, raw p, BH-adjusted p across the 50 sets, ranked by adjusted p. Complement with a non-parametric check — Wilcoxon rank-sum per pathway with BH correction — and report agreement between the two, since n=6 per group is small enough that the moderated-t normality assumption is worth cross-checking. Produce a bar or lollipop plot of the top differentially active hallmark sets by signed mean difference, coloured by FDR significance, and a per-sample dot/violin plot of scores for the top 6 pathways so that within-group spread and any sample_01 effect are visible. Additionally, repeat the limma contrast with sample_01 excluded and report whether the significant set changes — a sensitivity analysis, not the primary result.
acceptance_criteria: Results table for every scored hallmark set with per-condition mean score, mean difference, moderated t statistic, raw p and BH-adjusted p, sorted by adjusted p, written to disk
Wilcoxon rank-sum results reported alongside limma, with the degree of agreement between the two stated
Number of hallmark sets passing FDR < 0.05 reported explicitly, including when that number is zero
Plot of top differentially active hallmark sets by signed mean difference with FDR significance encoded, plus per-sample score plots for the top pathways showing all 12 individual samples
Leave-sample_01-out sensitivity analysis reported: which pathways enter or leave the FDR-significant set
The direction of every reported difference is stated relative to the literal condition labels in metadata.csv (which group is higher)

plan.title: UC inflamed vs control hallmark GSVA sample scores
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark heatmap that shows which pathways separate UC inflamed colon from control. That is a sample-level gene-set scoring problem, not a gene-level DE problem, so the analysis is organised around GSVA on a variance-stabilised expression matrix rather than around a DESeq2 gene list. Three steps.

T1S1 prepares the matrix: counts.csv is 12,000 genes x 12 samples (13 columns = gene symbol + 12 samples) of raw Salmon gene-level integer counts, and metadata.csv carries one condition column over 12 samples (6 UC inflamed, 6 control, unpaired, single batch). The profile flags sample_01 with a library size roughly 4x below the median — this matters more for GSVA than for DESeq2, because GSVA scores a per-sample expression profile directly and a shallow library inflates the fraction of zero/low counts, which distorts the within-sample gene ranking GSVA depends on. The step therefore filters low-expressed genes on a CPM basis, applies DESeq2 VST (library-size aware, variance-stabilising, appropriate for n=12), and documents sample_01's post-normalisation position in PCA and in a per-sample distribution summary so downstream interpretation knows whether it behaves as an outlier. Duplicate gene symbols are collapsed here because GSVA requires unique row identifiers.

T1S2 is the deliverable itself: GSVA (Gaussian kernel CDF, the correct kernel for continuous VST data) over the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets, giving a 50 x 12 score matrix — one score per pathway per sample — written as CSV, plus the requested heatmap with samples column-annotated by condition. Rows are clustered so co-moving pathways group; a column dendrogram shows whether the samples separate by condition without being told to.

T1S3 asks the statistical question the heatmap only suggests: which hallmark scores actually differ between UC inflamed and control. limma on the GSVA score matrix is the standard test for enrichment scores (they are continuous and roughly Gaussian, not counts), with BH FDR across the 50 sets. With 6 vs 6 this is modest power, so the step reports effect sizes alongside adjusted p-values and is explicit that GSVA-then-test on the same samples is descriptive ranking rather than independent validation.
